I farm only 4.1 mu, and I do the work myself, so I will keep the plan simple and manageable. I will stay with cotton on the full area because that is what I know best after 40 years, and on a small farm I do not want to take risks with a new crop. Since it is the start of the growing season and I have well irrigation, I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed so I can get steadier emergence and better yield without making management too complicated. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and easier for me than deeper ploughing every year.

For fertilizer, I will use a moderate but solid rate: enough nitrogen to support vegetative growth, with phosphorus and potassium to support root development, boll setting, and overall plant strength. I will not push fertilizer too hard because my area is small and I want a reliable crop, not excessive cost or rank growth. Since I have access to a well, I will irrigate several times through the season, mainly around establishment, flowering, and boll development, because cotton responds well when water is available at the right stages. I will also plan for several pesticide sprays, because cotton usually needs insect control and I would rather protect yield than wait too long and lose the crop. With my experience and irrigation access, I will aim for a stable medium-to-good yield instead of chasing the highest possible output.
